articles.title: Donald Trump’s Korea Diplomacy Is a Distraction Exercise
articles.author: Kap Seol
articles.content_excerpt: Donald Trump has made several recent overtures to North Korean leader Kim Jong-un for a new summit, seven years after their meeting in Hanoi ended inconclusively. Over the summer, he abruptly reduced the scale of the annual US–South Korea joint military exercises. Four times in the space of nine days, he posted pictures of Kim on his Truth Social account in an apparent wooing exercise. These efforts have so far failed to lure Kim to the negotiation table. Kim Yo-jong, his powerful sister who occupies the number-two position in the North Korean hierarchy, declared on August 19 that North Korea has no interest in a new summit with the United States. articles.title: An Agenda for De-Alienating Work
articles.author: Peter Dorman
articles.content_excerpt: Wages have been bad for years, but the quality of work hasn’t fared much better. Gig work, with its insecurity and minimal protection from managerial whims, has proliferated. New technology has enabled a degree of workforce surveillance that previous generations would have regarded as unacceptable. The degradation of corporate work at all levels is an important aspect of enshittification . Unsurprisingly, you can now click across multiple websites advising you how to look like you’re doing your job when your brain is somewhere else. And now AI is poised to usher us — those who still have jobs — into a new era of management-by-slop. Where can we look for an agenda to fight back? There’s a branch of left-wing thought that focuses on exactly these kinds of problems: the theory of alienation.

articles.title: Jean-Luc Mélenchon Thinks He Has a Path to Victory
articles.author: Olly Haynes
articles.content_excerpt: High above the waters of the Lac d’Aiguille in southeastern France, hundreds of drones formed the face of Maximilien Robespierre, the Jacobin deputy to the National Convention during the French Revolution. Then they shifted into a new form, as the face of Louise Michel, a key figure in the Paris Commune of 1871. The drones then split up again, only to regroup as the face of Thomas Sankara, the revolutionary leader of Burkina Faso. The music playing from the lakeside speakers sped up, and two drones dropped a banner, onto which was projected video from an accelerating series of rallies and speeches by France Insoumise (FI) and its presidential candidate Jean-Luc Mélenchon. articles.title: Gloria Steinem Was the Godmother of Neoliberal Feminism
articles.author: Jenny Brown
articles.content_excerpt: Gloria Steinem, the establishment’s favorite radical feminist, died on September 2. The mainstream media has gone all out in praising her, with the Wall Street Journal and The New York Times united in their adulation. The Times called her the “personification of the women’s movement” and credited her with helping to usher in “sweeping cultural transformations across virtually every facet of American life, from the boardroom to the courtroom to the bedroom.” They approvingly quote her self-description as an “entrepreneur of social change.” For many people, she is the only radical feminist they can name, eclipsing the extraordinary women who planned and launched the successful women’s liberation movement starting in 1967. articles.title: Organizing from the Bottom: IBEW’s Fight for Sanitary Facilities
articles.author: Detroit DSA
articles.content_excerpt: Workers in high-visibility gear gather at a downtown Detroit worksite, with the city skyline visible in the background. By Kevin Szczesny To get clean Porta-johns in our workplace, construction workers at the Marriott site in downtown Detroit marched on the boss. Workers from at least seven unions of the building trades were represented, with zero union staffers or officers present. Many union halls were in support of the action, but the work and the application of leverage were entirely rank-and-file driven. As an active member of IBEW Local 58 (Electrical Workers), I often hear from sympathetic organizers who “can’t imagine how hard it must be” organizing in a largely conservative and obstinate workforce.
